issues.description: The core loop still iterates all pairs (u in 1..N1) × (v in N1+1..N1+N2). This is O(N1 * N2) and will TLE for the problem constraints (up to ~2.25e10 pairs). The correct, efficient approach is to take the farthest distance in the first subset (max dist_from_1) and the farthest distance in the second subset (max dist_from_N1N2) and return max1 + 1 + max2 — no nested pairwise loop is needed. As implemented, the solution is functionally correct on small inputs but will not finish on large inputs (observed TLE).

No tests were provided with the submission. At least one large/randomized test covering worst-case sizes or the sample cases should accompany the fix to prevent regressions and to demonstrate the TLE is resolved.

The code builds an existing_edges set and checks for (min(u,v), max(u,v)) membership inside the nested loop. Given the problem guarantees that vertex 1 and vertex N1+N2 are initially disconnected and that each group is connected, there cannot be any cross-group edges initially — so that set and check are unnecessary overhead. Simplifying the logic by removing this will reduce noise and micro-cost.

The top-of-file platform import block (included by the platform) causes a ruff warning about imports not at top-level for the rest of the file; this is an environmental artifact and not part of the submitted algorithm. It can be ignored for correctness but explains the static-analysis message seen in the pipeline.
